title: How the sheet should come up
variant: A motion on a spring, with the CSS it settles into as the takeaway
prompt: We keep arguing about how the bottom sheet should animate in. Can you build something we can play with until it feels right, and that gives us the CSS?
note: The motion shape, and the one that shows why the template defaults to dialkit: its spring editor draws the curve, and the reader can switch it between a visual duration and a bounce, raw physics, and a hand-shaped bezier, so the page has to write honest CSS for all three. The stage is a phone with a real sheet on it, animated through the browser's animation API with the same linear() easing the reader copies, so the preview is the CSS rather than an approximation of it. Bounce and duration become stiffness and damping by Motion's own formula, read from its source rather than remembered, and settled is Motion's rule too, which is why the page can state it in its last line and a reader can check the 800 ms. The three figures beside the phone are arithmetic over the dials and nothing else: how long it takes, how far it overshoots, and the damping ratio with a word that says what it means. The panel has no Reset of its own, so the page carries one. Offline, the column where the dials would be lists the opening settings in words and the sheet still comes up.
